articles.title: Will Brock Bowers play today? New injury report on Raiders tight end
articles.summary: Will Brock Bowers play against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday? Here's the latest injury report on the Las Vegas Raiders tight end.
articles.body:
Sunday morning reports indicate that Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers will play today against the New Orleans Saints . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Bowers is expected to play, barring a surprise. Brock Bowers has missed the first two games of the year with a knee injury and has been listed as questionable this week despite not practicing Friday. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. The Raiders may have tipped their hand by not elevating practice squad tight end Chris Myarick , who was brought up for each of the first two games while Bowers was on the mend.

Bowers was the 13th choice in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft from the Georgia Bulldogs. As a rookie, he had 112 receptions for 1,194 yards and 5 touchdowns. Injuries caused him to miss five games in 2025, but he'd still have 680 receiving yards with a team-best 64 catches and 7 scores.

Without Bowers, 2023 second-round draft pick Michael Mayer has taken a central role at tight end. Mayer has 9 receptions for 55 yards so far. Over his first three seasons, Mayer averaged 28 catches for 263 yards. Mayer is a more traditional tight end with good physicality and route running skills. Bowers provides an athletic mismatch for defenses and is a threat from multiple spots in an offensive formation.

The 2-0 Raiders play at the 1-1 New Orleans Saints this afternoon. New Orleans has had trouble containing opposing tight ends. In Week 1, Detroit 's Sam LaPorta caught 5 passes on 8 targets for 48 yards, doing most of his damage in the first half. Last week, Mark Andrews of Baltimore caught 6 of his 7 targets for 49 yards.

articles.title: Alabama TE Josh Ford reacts after Dylan Stewart punches him: 'It was awesome'
articles.summary: Alabama tight end Josh Ford addressed the punch he took from South Carolina edge rusher Dylan Stewart on Saturday. Here's what he said.
articles.body:
Alabama stomped South Carolina on Saturday night in Tuscaloosa behind Keelon Russell 's breakout SEC performance, where he threw for nearly 400 yards and four touchdowns.

It led to frustration for Shane Beamer's Gamecocks , specifically edge rusher Dylan Stewart , who, in the fourth quarter, punched the helmet of Crimson Tide tight end Josh Ford in the end zone after Daniel Hill ran in a 1-yard touchdown run that stretched the score to a 24-point lead with 6:43 remaining in the game.

"Man, he's a great player. We had a lot of fun today. I think he punched me three times, but it was awesome, it was a good battle," Ford said after the game.

ESPN rules analyst Jerry McGinn said Stewart should've been ejected for the punch. Instead of being ejected, Stewart was only hit with an unsportsmanlike penalty.

"He should be ejected immediately," McGinn said on the broadcast. "Not even a question."

Earlier in the game, ESPN's broadcast caught Beamer yelling at Stewart on the Gamecocks' sidelines for either slowly walking off the field or not getting off fast enough, as noted by The Greenville News, part of the USA TODAY Network. That heated moment came after Stewart was called for a roughing-the-passer penalty, which eventually led to a 42-yard touchdown reception from Ryan Coleman-Williams.

Stewart finished with no recorded tackles or sacks in the Gamecocks' 49-18 loss to the Crimson Tide on the road.

With the win, Alabama heads into its highly anticipated Week 5 matchup against Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State with a 2-0 record in SEC play.

articles.title: As 49ers injuries pile up, WR Mike Evans reportedly set to play vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Evans missed two practices this week with a hip injury.
articles.body:
A flurry of defensive lineman and wide receiver injuries have already decimated the San Francisco 49ers this year. But at least for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Arizona Cardinals , star wide receiver Mike Evans is expected to be on the field.

According to ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler , Evans plans to play through the hip injury he suffered in Week 2's blowout win over the Dolphins. Evans was listed as questionable after he didn't practice at all on Wednesday and Thursday and was a limited participant on Friday.

It's a piece of good news for San Francisco in the face of so many other injury issues. Earlier this week, star defensive end Nick Bosa injured his calf warming up for practice on Thursday and is now expected to miss a few weeks. That injury, added in with so many others on the defensive line, led the Niners to work out four veteran pass rushers on Saturday - not a thing you want to be doing before a Week 3 game.

"Losing six out of the 10 D-linemen in the last two weeks that have made our team is a little unusual," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan admitted in a press conference on Friday. "I don't think I've been a part of that, so that has been different."

The only other position that's been as impacted by injuries is wide receiver. The 49ers have already lost Ricky Pearsall for the season with a knee injury, won't have top 2026 draft pick De'Zhaun Stribling for at least the next two months with an ankle injury and placed veteran Demarcus Robinson on injured reserve on Saturday with a high ankle sprain.

Evans was already banged up quite a bit this season, missing time in training camp with a quad strain, a foot injury and a pulled groin. But Evans suited up in the first two games and shined , catching 9-of-10 passes thrown his way for 103 yards and a touchdown. Shanahan said Evans has been "everything as advertised as a person and a player" on Friday.

The 33-year-old is in his first year with the 49ers after spending the rest of his career in Tampa Bay. Evans set an NFL record by hauling in at least 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first 11 seasons, also tying Niners legend Jerry Rice for the most consecutive years, period. But Evans' streak ended last season after he missed eight games with a broken collarbone, hamstring injury and a concussion.

The 49ers, with Evans expected to suit up, will kick off against the Cardinals at 1:05 p.m. on Sunday, with the game televised on Fox.

articles.title: Salient Stats: LSU 35, Texas A&M 6
articles.summary: The numbers that tell the tale of the Aggies embarrassing loss to LSU
articles.body:
It's not exactly difficult to find stats that are salient in this one. The Tigers dominated the Aggies in pretty much every category imaginable in a game that only further reinforced that this 2026 Texas A&M squad is simply, and inexplicably, not good whatsoever.

0: Sacks for the A&M defense. A&M's secondary play has been pretty bad, and has been made to look even worse by A&M's inability to get consistent pressure on the QB. There is so much blame to go around on this team's underachievement.

8: Regular season games remaining, which almost feels like a punishment at this point.

4.5: Texas A&M's yards per carry if you take out Marcel Reed . The run game that was so critiqued early in the season is actually coming along nicely. But a combination of poor pass protection and Marcel Reed's inability to hit open receivers on a regular basis rendered it moot for the second straight week.

31.3: QBR for Marcel Reed. That was 105th out of 129 FBS QBs this week, with only four P4 QBs performing worse. Reed has yet to be ranked in the top half of FBS QBs in any week this season.

51.9/54: Average yards per punt from Tyler White (51.9) and the long field goal absolutely drilled by David Olano (54). It's a shame that A&M seemed to solve their kicking woes from last season on to see pretty much every other aspect of the team regress.

69.9: The highest PFF rating for any A&M offensive player on Saturday night. That's, uh, that's really really bad y'all.

100%: Interception rate for backup QB Brady Hart on Saturday night. Obviously he was inserted late into a bad situation, but having your only pass attempted picked off underscores the point that as bad as Marcel Reed has been, the Aggies likely don't have a better option on the bench either. Hard to believe A&M coaches let the QB room get to this point.

309: Total yardage advantage. No, I don't mean LSU had 309 total yards. I mean they had 309 MORE yards than A&M. Simply unacceptable play on both sides of the ball.

articles.title: Matt Campbell searches for positive spin on stunning loss to Wisconsin
articles.summary: Penn State fans could be questioning coach Matt Campbell after his postgame comments following a loss to Wisconsin.
articles.body:
For many Penn State fans, they will be looking for answers to an inexplicable loss to Wisconsin . Most would say those answers would come from new head coach Matt Campbell. The reason for a large portion of Penn State fans' transparency in the last stages of the Franklin era was due to the lack of ownership, leadership, and being up front about issues facing the prorgam. They thought they were getting better with Matt Campbell. Turns out it may just be the same old story.

Instead of completely owning the loss and taking the blame, moving forward to the next week, Matt Campbell instead decided to take a more positive spin. When asked about the play of his quarterback, Campbell avoided being critical in the immediate aftermath of the Saturday evening loss

"It'll be interesting to answer that question even a little bit better after you watch the videotape. But I thought Rocco made some tremendous plays," Campbell said when asked to evaluate the play of his quarterback, Rocco Becht . "I thought he kept us in the football game. Some scrambles at the time, maybe some scrambles and throws".

I think not many Penn State fans, myself included, would agree with that statement. Rocco Becht in his first Big Ten game went 12-of-29 for only 129 yards. Sure, the tipped interception could be excused, but there were far more mistakes from Becht that you should not want to see out of the most experienced college QB in the nation, as the Peacock broadcast pointed out on numerous occasions. There were blatant missed throws and tons of miscommunication issues with his receivers. Most importantly, the previously unflappable Becht looked rattled at various key moments.

Most surprising were Campbell's comments on the overall flow of the game.

"I think there was just a weird flow to the game, especially in the first half of the football game, where you're in more situational football," Campbell said in his postgame press conference. "I think some of it will be really interesting to see what happened in the second half. I think I'll have a better answer for you guys on Tuesday to that question," Campbell said.

While some might see his comments on Becht as defending his QB, these could be seen as more inexcusable. As the head coach, you're supposed to have answers for everything, not just off the field, but on it. The fact that Campbell can't quite explain what transpired from the first half to the second is not encouraging, but truly worrying. The bottom line is that while Campbell should not fear for his job, comments like this have become too much of a theme for Penn State over the last couple of years, whether it be from Franklin's mouth or his.

articles.title: FanDuel: Illinois opens as 9.5-point favorite against Purdue
articles.summary: The sportsbooks like the Illini.
articles.body:
After a difficult road trip to Columbus, Illinois will return home for a Big Ten matchup with Purdue as both teams search for their first conference win of 2026.

FanDuel Sportsbook has already released its opening odds for the matchup, and the oddsmakers have Illinois favored by nearly double digits.

Illinois is also a significant favorite on the moneyline at -385, while Purdue is listed at +300.

The over/under for the matchup is set at 59.5 points, with the over priced at -106 and the under at -114. That total implies a projected final score of roughly 35-25 in favor of Illinois. It's not quite the fireworks (and theatrics) of the 50-49 win Illinois had over the Boilers the last time they played in Champaign in 2024, but still high-scoring!

The Illini enter the matchup at 2-2 following Saturday's 42-19 loss to No. 7 Ohio State in Columbus when Jeremiah Smith caught a career-high four touchdowns, including three in the first half. Illinois opened the season with wins over UAB and Southern Illinois, while its other loss came against Duke.

Purdue, meanwhile, entered Week 4 with a 1-2 record after opening the season with a win over Indiana State before dropping consecutive games to Wake Forest and UCLA. The Boilermakers then got to host Notre Dame, and the Fighting Irish routed them 49-10.

Illinois has won back-to-back Cannons, including the aforementioned dramatic 2024 showdown and a 43-27 win in West Lafayette last season.

This year's matchup will be Illinois' Homecoming game and is scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT on Saturday, Oct. 3, at Gies Memorial Stadium. The game will be broadcast on the Big Ten Network.

So who are you taking? Do you trust the Illini's defense enough to get some stops and pull out a win? Or is there big trouble in Champaign? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Is Puka Nacua playing today vs. Broncos? Latest on Rams WR’s status

articles.body:
Puka Nacua missed the Los Angeles Rams ' Week 2 win against the New York Giants due to a hip injury after going into the game with a questionable tag. Ahead of tonight's matchup with the Denver Broncos , Nacua is officially listed as doubtful to play.

Players listed as doubtful rarely end up playing, but what's the latest on Nacua for tonight against the Broncos? Adam Schefter of ESPN shared an update on Sunday morning, which comes with some disappointing news for tonight but optimism for next week against the Eagles .

Nacua didn't practice at all this past week but there's were videos of him running and sprinting off to the side with trainers. That's a good sign for his progress, which is likely why the Rams are optimistic he can play next week in Philadelphia .

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy, Justin Fields among 6 QBs New York Giants are considering
articles.summary: The New York Giants are reportedly considering six quarterbacks, including J.J. McCarthy and Justin Fields.
articles.body:
Jameis Winston gets the keys Sunday against the Tennessee Titans , and the New York Giants are already glancing at the spare set.

Jaxson Dart underwent surgery on Friday to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee, ending his season. Head coach John Harbaugh left a sliver of hope for a playoff return, but the immediate job belongs to Winston.

Thrown into a plan built for Dart on Monday night, Winston went 11 of 27 for 111 yards with an interception in a 28-6 loss to the Rams . New York spent the week rewriting the menu around a pocket passer instead of a dual-threat.

How hard the Giants push for another quarterback will depend, in part, on what Winston does at a windy, rainy Meadowlands. Jake Haener was signed off the practice squad on Saturday to back him up. Harbaugh said all options remain open.

Garoppolo is the simplest add because he would not cost a draft pick. His camp has spoken with New York this week, though he has not worked out. After flirting with retirement, he wants a 53-man roster spot rather than the practice squad.

Minshew played for offensive coordinator Matt Nagy in Kansas City , and Fields is in a similar system now. Jones went 5-3 last year filling in for Brock Purdy . McCarthy sits third in Minnesota, and the Giants have been doing their homework.

Sunday is Winston's first real audition of the post-Dart era. The shopping list is already printed.

articles.title: Mr. Olympia 2026 Results, Final Prize Money, Highlights for Nick Walker and Top Stars
articles.summary: Nick Walker is your 2026 Mr. Olympia. The 32-year-old pro from New Jersey made a memorable run at the Olympia Open, a year after a disappointing sixth-place finish.
articles.body:
Nick Walker is your 2026 Mr. Olympia. The 32-year-old pro from New Jersey made a memorable run at the Olympia Open, a year after a disappointing sixth-place finish.

There were signs during the IFBB season that Walker could be making his way to the top. The relatively compact (5'7") competitor showed improved definition in his midsection while notching a second-place finish at the Arnold Classic and winning the Tampa Pro.

It quickly became clear during Friday's prejudging that bringing a new and refined look to the Olympia stage. Would it be enough to unseat the reigning champion, Derek Lunsford?

By late Saturday evening, fans had their answer.

2026 Mr. Olympia Open Results and Payout

Fans got an idea of who might have a shot at the finals during Friday night's prejudging.

The first callout of the night featured Andrew Jacked, Tonio Burton, Michal Krizanek, Samson Dauda, Lunsford, and Walker. Jacked, Dauda, Walker, and Lunsford made up the final callout.

With the field narrowed to 10 finalists by Saturday, each competitor got the opportunity to impress judges with a three-minute individual routine. It became even clearer than it was on Friday that there would be no obvious winner.

Lunsford was looking to defend his crown and win his third Sandow Trophy in four years. He provided the first bar that Walker needed to clear.

Walker also had to contend with Jacked, the 2026 Arnold Classic winner, and 2024 Mr. Olympia, Dauda. The latter immediately looked to be the bigger challenge, in the literal sense.

Dauda came in off a win at the 2026 Europa Pro in Germany. However, competing just two weeks before the Olympia raised questions about his ability to arrive in peak conditioning. Nevertheless, Dauda was in championship form and easily could have taken the top spot.

More than a few fans probably came away from Saturday night believing that Dauda deserved to claim his second Olympia title in three years. An argument could certainly be made that Dauda and Jacked overshadowed most of the other competitors with size alone.

Ultimately, though, career-best conditioning from Walker was enough to win the Open, along with a strong final stage performance.

Tonio Burton, who won this year's New York Pro, rounded out the top five.

Walker will undoubtedly enjoy his victory for some time, though he and the other top competitors are likely already devising their strategies for next season. He'll look to become the first back-to-back champion since Mamdouh Elssbiay hoisted the Sandow in 2020 and 2021.
